question: Which of the following gives the correct decreasing order of the densities of a soil sample?
explanation: Let the volume of saturated soil = Volume of wet soil 83. = Volume of dry soil. Hence, higher is the mass of soil higher will be its density. Now, In saturated soil, since voids are completely filled with water hence mass of soil is very high. In wet soil, voids are partially filled with water hence mass of wet soil is less than saturated. In dry soil, voids are filled with air only hence mass of soil is less than wet and saturated. In submerged soil, As per Archimedes Principle, the mass of soil is very less than wet, dry and saturated. Hence decreasing order, γsaturated > γwet > γdry > γsubmerged

question: The minimum water content at which the soil just begins to crumble when rolled into threads 3 mm in diameter, is known as
explanation: The minimum water content at which the soil just begins to crumble when rolled into threads 3mm in diameter is known as plastic limit. Shrinkage limit–Shrinkage limit is the water content at which the soil stop shrinkage further and attains a constant volume. Shrinkage limit– Shrinkage limit defined as that maximum water content at which further reduction in water content does not cause reduction in the volume of soil sample is called shrinkage. Shrinkage limit may also be defined as the lowest water content at which the soil is just saturated. Below the shrinkage limit, the soil does not remain saturated. Air enters the voids of the soil. Liquid Limit– Minimum water content at which soil has a tendency to flow is called liquid limit water content. All soils at liquid limit will have similar shear strength which is negligible i.e. 2.7 kN/m2 Plastic limit– Minimum water content at which soil is in plastic stage is called plastic limit water content. At plastic limit water content, a soil rolled into a thread of 3 mm starts to crumble. 364. question: Which one of the clay mineral has expansive properties ?
explanation: Montmorillonite • Montmorillonite is 2:1 clay mineral as it is composed of 2 silica sheet and 1 Alumina (Gibbsite) sheet. • Montmorillonite has large specific surface amongst clay minerals. • Montmorillonite has large amount of water and other exchangable ions can easily enter between the layers causing the layers to be seperated. Because of this property it is susceptible to substantial volume change and highly active. • Montmorillonite is found in black cotton soil and Bentonite is a montmorillonite clay. Kaolinite: • Kaolinite consists of structure based on single sheet of silica combined with single sheet of gibbsite. The combined silica gibbsite sheet are held together strongly by hydrogen bond which is very strong. • Water cannot easily enter between the structural units and cannot cause swelling hence activity of this clay mineral is least. 174 • it is often called as 1:1 clay mineral. Held by Hydrogen bond (very strong) between OH– of Alumina sheet and O–2 of silica sheet. Illite: • Illite is a 2:1 clay mineral. • Illite has substantial amount of isomorphous substitution in the form of 'Al' in place of 'Si'. • 'K+' bonds the two negative surfaces of silica sheet tightly. • This potassium ion bond the layer more firmly than montmorillonite. Thus it is much less susceptible to cleavage or splitting. • Illite does not swell much in presence of water like montmorillonite. But it swells more than kaolinite. • It is common in stiff clays and in lacustrine soft clay.
source: UPPSC State Eng. A.E. 2007(II)] [UPPSC State Eng. A.E. 2003 · Civil Engg. Vol-1 p.174

question: Statement (I): Saturated fine, as well as medium, sands of uniform particle size are most susceptible to liquefaction. Statement (II): Fine particles reduce the permeability which is a prime factor for liquefaction.
options: Both Statements-I and Statement-II are individually true and Statement-II is the correct explanation of Statement-I.
Both Statements-I and Statement-II are individually true but Statement-II is NOT the correct explanation of Statement-I
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
explanation: If rate of loading is larger and soil is saturated +ve pore water pressure will develop. This will reduce effective stress and hence strength. If effective stress reduce to zero the soil will loose all its shear strength. This phenomenon is known as liquefaction. Presence of fine particle reduces the permeability. Thus, it will increase the chance of liquefaction as dissipation of excess pore water pressure become more difficult.

question: The changes that take place during the process of consolidation of a saturated clay would include
options: an increase in pore water pressure and an increase in effective pressure
an increase in pore water pressure and a decrease in effective pressure
a decrease in pore water pressure and a decrease in effective pressure
a decrease in pore water pressure and an increase in effective pressure
explanation: When the load is applied to the saturated clay mass, the whole applied pressure (stress) is taken up by water as an excess pore water pressure. Effective stress = Total stress – Pore pressure. Hence effective stress does not change initially. How, during the process of consolidation, with the expulsion of pore water, the pore water pressure decreases and thus effective stress increases. At the end of consolidation pore water pressure reduces to zero and the whole stress is taken up by the soil grains.

question: Which of the following is not an assumption in terzhaghi’s formulation of bearing capacity equation?
options: Base of the footing is smooth
The width of the base of the footing is less than or equal to the founding depth
Shear strength is governed by Mohr- Coulomb failure criteria
explanation: Assumption in terzhaghi's formula: (1) footing is located at a depth Df below the ground surface such that Df ≤B, where B is the width of the footing. This means he considered the foundation to be shallow. (2) Footing is continuous, this makes the analysis two dimensional. (3) Base of foundation is rough (4) The angle of roughness between base of footing and for soil is considered equal to friction angle of the soil. (5) failure is general shear failure and at the time of failure soil reaches into plastic state. (6) the soil above the base of the footing is replaced by on equivalent surcharge (q = γDf). This means that 1340. shearing resistance of the soil located above the base is neglected however for dip foundation it can not be neglected. (7) the stress zone of the soil extends upto foundation level and not upto ground level.
source: UPRVUNL AE 2016 · Civil Engg. Vol-1 p.302
bookUnit: Geo-technical Engineering and Foundation Engineering (Soil Mechanics)

question: The maximum stress that can be applied to a material for an infinite number of cycles of repeated stress without causing failure is called
explanation: Endurance Limit : It is the stress level below which even large number of stress cycle can not produce fatigue failure. Proportional Limit – Proportional limit determines the greatest stress that is directly proportional to strain. Elastic limit– Maximum stress or force per unit area within a solid material that can arise before the permanent deformation, when stresses upto the elastic limit are removed, the material resumes its original size and shape, stresses beyond the elastic limit cause a material to yield or flow. Ultimate Strength– Ultimate strength of a material in tension, compression or shear, respectively is the maximum tensile, compressive or shear stress that the material can sustain, calculated on the basis of the ultimate load and the original or unstrained dimensions.

question: The stress at which a material fractures under large number of reversal of stresses is called:
explanation: Endurance limit – Endurance limit is the stress level below which a specimen can withstand cyclic stress (reversal of stress) indefinitely without exhibiting fatigue failure. Residual stress – Residual stresses are stresses that remain in a solid material after the original cause of the stresses has been removed. Creep – creep is the tendency of a solid material to move slowly and deform permanently under the influence of persistent mechanical stress. Ultimate stress – Ultimate stress is the maximum value of stress that a material can resist.

question: Castigliano's first theorem is applicable-
options: Only when principle of superposition is valid
explanation: Castigliano's first theorem is applicable only when principle of superposition is valid. Castigliano's first theorem : The first partial derivative of the total internal energy (strain energy) in a structure with respect to any particular deflection component at a point is equal to the force applied at that point and in the direction corresponding to that deflection component. This first theorem is applicable to linearly or non- linearly elastic structures in which the temperature is constant and the supports are unyielding. Castigliano's second theorem : The first partial derivative of the total internal energy (strain energy) in a structure with respect to the force applied at any point is equal to the deflection at the point of application of that force in the direction of its line of action. The second theorem of Castigliano's is applicable to linearly elastic (Hookean material) structures with constant temperature and unyielding supports. 534. Moderate Sheltered from severe rain or freezing whilst wet, or exposed to condensation and rain, or continuously under water, or in contact with or buried under non- aggressive solid or ground water, or sheltered from saturated 'salt air' in coastal area. Severe Exposed to severe rain, alternate wetting and drying or occasional freezing whilst wet or severe condensation, or completely immersed in sea water, or exposed to coastal environment. question: Which of the following types of failures occur in the beam-column connections ? 1. Failure by lateral - torsional buckling 2. Failure by combined instability in both the principal directions 3. Failure by combined twisting and bending on the torsionally weak sections 4. Failure by combined twisting and bending when plane of bending does not contain the shear centre.
explanation: Beam-column is a structural member subjected to both axial compression and bending moment with likely mode of failures may exist, which are : (1) Failure by instability in plane of bending without twisting under axial compression and bending about one axis. (2) Failure by lateral torsional buckling under axial compression and bending about the major axis. (3) Failure by instability in one of the principal direction due to axial compression and biaxial bending (torsionally stiff section) (4) Failure by combined twisting and bending on torsionally weak section (thin walled section). (5) Failure by combined twisting and bending when plane of bending does not contain the shear centre under axial compression, biaxial bending and torsion.

The material used in the construction of movement joint should not slump unduly in hot weather or become brittle in cold weather.
explanation: Design of a movement joint should aim at following desirable properties for its efficient functioning : (a) The joint should accommodate repeated movement of the structure without loss of water tightness. (b) The design should provide for exclusion of grit and debris which would prevent the closing of the joint. (c) The material used in the construction of movement joints should have the following properties– (1) It should not suffer permanent distortion or extrusion and should not be displaced by fluid pressure. (2) It should not slump unduly in hot weather or become brittle in cold weather. (3) It is should be insoluble and durable and should not be affected by exposure to light or by evaporation of solvent or plasticizers. (4) In special cases, the material should be non- toxic, taintless or resistant to chemical and biological action as may be specified.

question: The method of pre-stressing concrete in which pre-stressing steel is tensioned against the hardened concrete is:
explanation: The method of pre-stressing concrete in which pre-stressing steel is tensional against the hardened concrete is post tensioning. Pre-tensioning : In pre-tensioning system the high strength steel tendons are pulled between two end abutments prior to the casting of concrete and the abutments are fixed at the ends of pre-stressing bed. Once the concrete attains the desired strength for pre- stressing the tendons are cut loose from the abutments. 908 Post-tensioning : In post tensioning systems the ducts for the tendons are placed along with the reinforcement before the casting of concrete. The tendons are placed in the ducts after casting of concrete. The duct prevents contact between concrete and the tendons during the tensioning operation.

subject: Civil Engineering Core
question: What is the area of building, excluding the area occupied by walls?
explanation: Net area- Net area is the area required for specific uses such as; classrooms, offices etc. It is measured to the interior face of enclosing wall. Plinth area- Plinth area is the covered built-up area measured at the floor level of any story. Carpet area- It is internal measure required to lay carpet which obviously does not include the thickness of wall. Floor area- It is the area calculated by multiplying the outer to outer dimension of floor, not consider the boundary wall, but include the outer and inner wall of building.
